title: New Tariffs Could Raise Costs for American Shoppers
summary:
The Trump administration has announced plans for a new round of tariffs — taxes on goods imported from other countries — that could raise prices for American shoppers. The plan would cover China, the European Union, and 12 other major trading partners. China would face the highest rate, a new 20 percent tariff on most products. That would sit on top of existing levels, adding up to a possible 40 percent tariff if negotiations fall apart. Other countries would face 10 to 20 percent in additional tariffs. The new tariffs could go into effect as soon as January. U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said the goal is to protect manufacturing in the United States. He said the U.S. should produce more of what it uses at home, arguing that other countries are building production capacity that is not justified by economics. The administration says the tariffs would be targeted, applying to a subset of goods from each country, while it also negotiates with those countries about excess capacity.

Gavin Bade of The Wall Street Journal, who first reported the plan, said the tariffs would matter a lot for what shoppers pay. The Yale Economic Lab estimated the tariffs would add another $400 for each American in general. The move comes after the Supreme Court ruled in February that many of the administration's earlier tariffs were illegal. Those tariffs had relied on the International Emergency Economic Powers Act, a law never before used for tariffs. This time, the administration is using a different legal authority, Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974, which deals with unfair trading practices. Bade said this approach has a much better chance of standing up in court. The administration argues that countries like China subsidize their industries, letting them flood world markets with very low-priced products. The tariff truce with China is supposed to end in January, and Bade said the 20 percent level is one the Chinese have expected for a long time.
why_it_matters: Tariffs can change the prices families pay for everyday things, so understanding them helps explain why shopping might get more expensive.

background_read: A tariff is a tax that a country puts on goods brought in from other countries, which can make those goods cost more for shoppers.
Countries use tariffs to protect their own factories and workers, hoping people will buy more things made at home.
Trading partners are countries that buy and sell a lot of goods from each other, and tariffs can change how much trade happens between them.
When a court rules that a law was not used correctly, the government may try again using a different law that fits the rules better.
